p002-u001: RoboMaster RMOC (RMOC, RoboMaster Organizing Committee) encourages and advocates technological innovation and technology open source, and respects the intellectual property rights of the participating team. All intellectual property rights developed by the participating team in the competition belong to the team. p010-u002: The National College Student Robot Competition RoboMaster University League (RMUL, RoboMaster University League) is initiated by DJI and hosted by local academic institutions and universities, drawing in surrounding universities to participate. It aims to promote regional exchange of university robotics technology, foster a strong academic atmosphere, and support regional scientific and technological innovation.
p010-u003: RMUL is committed to cultivating outstanding young engineers and encourages participating team members to combine the knowledge they have learned with practical applications and achieve continuous growth during the competition.
p010-u005: The RMUL 2027 season has two challenge events: the 3V3 Match and the Infantry Match.
p011-u001: In the 3V3 competition, both sides need to independently develop Heavy Robot, Infantry Robot and Sentry Robot, and conduct tactical confrontation by controlling the robots to launch projectiles to attack the opponent's robots in the designated Battlefield. At the end of the game, the team that controls Battlefield wins the game.
p011-u003: In the Infantry Match, each side must independently develop an Infantry Robot and control it to launch projectiles in a 1V1 confrontation on the designated Battlefield. When the match ends, the side whose Infantry Robot has more remaining HP wins.

p011-u012: Added the Heavy Robot special mechanism and Field Buffs mechanism, and adjusted the control zone and Control Points mechanisms.

p022-u006: The Custom Terminal (formerly the Custom Controller and Custom Client) is a multipurpose set of equipment built by participating teams. It monitors robot motion and status, controls robot actions, receives match-related information and robot camera video feeds sent by the Referee System’s match engine server, and sends match-specific interaction commands to that server to expand the possibilities for human-computer interaction.
p022-u007: A typical Custom Terminal may consist of a display device, a computing platform (including memory, controller and processor) and a set of input devices. It may also be integrated, such as a handheld tablet with a network port.
p022-u008: Example: A team builds a Custom Terminal that receives robot camera video and displays it on a self-made monitor. It overlays a self-made UI displayed through an unofficial link and controls the robot with a matching controller. As a result, the team can complete the match without using the official Referee System player terminal or Remote Controller.
p022-u009: Custom Terminals in the Operator Room can be connected to and communicate with each other by wire. They can also be wired to the match engine server and send and receive relevant content through the RJ45 interface in the Operator Room.
p022-u010: A Custom Terminal can receive match information shown on the Referee System player terminal and available to its user, such as both sides’ HP, the user’s own Economy, remaining match time and key match events.
p022-u011: A Custom Terminal can send match commands supported by the player terminal to the Referee System, such as selecting a Performance System before the match or redeeming Projectile Allowance during the match.

p036-u003: When a robot is Defeated, its Barrel Heat resets to 0 and its Buffer Energy resets to the Buffer Energy limit. A Defeated robot can be revived automatically after completing its revival progress. During automatic revival, progress increases by 1 point per second. The revival progress required for a robot’s first Defeat is 5; after each subsequent Defeat of the same robot, the required progress increases by 5.

p037-u020: There are three groups of control zones in the Battlefield, the red highland control zone, the blue highland control zone and the central control zone. After the game starts, the control zone mechanism takes effect.
p037-u022: At the start of the game, all three control zones are neutral.
p037-u023: Each party has its own independent "occupation progress" count for each control zone. The highest count is 5 and the lowest is 0. When a party's "occupation progress" of a control zone reaches 5, that party "controls" the control zone; when a party's "occupation progress" of a control zone is reduced to 0, that party loses control there. When neither party controls a control zone, the control zone is in a neutral state.
p037-u024: When a Control Zone is activated only by one side’s robot and the opposing side’s occupation progress is 0, the activating side’s occupation progress for that zone increases by 1 per second. When a Control Zone is activated only by one side’s robot and the opposing side’s occupation progress is not 0, the opposing side’s occupation progress for that zone decreases by 1 per second.
p037-u025: When both sides activate the same control zone, the change in occupation progress is suspended until only one robot remains active in the control zone.
p037-u026: When neither party activates a non-neutral control zone, both parties' occupation progress of the control zone will be reduced by 1 per second.
p038-u001: When the game starts, both sides have 600 Control Points:
p038-u003: For each Control Zone one side controls, the opposing side loses 1 Control Point per second.
p038-u005: Each time a robot on one side is Defeated, that side loses 10 Control Points.
p038-u006: When the difference in Control Points between the two sides is at least 200, the side with fewer Control Points needs 33% less Revival progress and its HP Recovery rate in the Supply Zone increases to 33%/s.
p038-u007: When the difference in Control Points between the two sides is at least 400, the side with fewer Control Points needs 50% less Revival progress and its HP Recovery rate in the Supply Zone increases to 50%/s.
p038-u010: Robots on both sides can activate both sides’ Highland Buff Points, and multiple robots on the same side can activate a Highland Buff Point simultaneously.
p038-u011: Robots that activate Highland Buff Point gain a 25% defense boost.
p038-u012: The highland Buff Point is also a highland control zone. For details on the control zone mechanism, see "3.3.4 Control Zone and Control Points Mechanism".
p038-u014: Each robot can activate its own tunnel Buff Point. Multiple robots on the same side can activate tunnel Buff Points at the same time.
p038-u015: When the same robot detects Field Interaction Module cards at two tunnel Buff Points in a Battlefield within 3 seconds, and no other Field Interaction Module cards are detected on the way, it can obtain a 1.5x heat cooling gain for 60 seconds.
p038-u017: Robots on both sides can activate Control Zones, and multiple robots on the same side can activate a Control Zone simultaneously. For the specific effects, see ‘3.3.4 Control Zones and Control Points Mechanism’.
p038-u018: After the robot does not detect the Field Interaction Module card of Buff Point, the activation status will expire after 2 seconds.
p038-u020: At the start of a match, the Heavy Robot’s performance attributes are low. To improve them, it must install the modular 42mm launching mechanism and launch a 42mm projectile correctly detected by the Referee System. For details on performance attributes, see ‘3.1.1 Heavy Robot’.
p038-u021: The Heavy Robot can perform the following operations, but only at the Workbench:

p039-u002: When the Heavy Robot has not successfully completed installation of the modular 42mm launching mechanism and activates its own Supply Zone, it is Invincible.
p039-u004: The 3V3 competition is divided into group round-robin and knockout. The format of the group round robin is BO2 and the knockout format is BO3.
p039-u005: The following are the winning conditions for a single game:
p039-u007: When one side’s Control Points reach 0, the round ends immediately and the side whose Control Points are not 0 wins.
p039-u009: When the Round time expires and neither side’s Control Points are 0, the side with more Control Points wins.
p039-u011: When the Round time expires and both sides have the same nonzero Control Points, the side with greater total Attack Damage wins.
p039-u013: When the Round time expires and both sides have the same nonzero Control Points and equal total Attack Damage, the side with greater total remaining HP across its robots wins.
p039-u015: If the above conditions cannot determine victory, the game will be deemed a draw. In the event of a tie in the knockout rounds, an extra round will be played immediately until a winner is determined.

p041-u010: Custom Terminal (original custom controller and custom client) is a set of multi-purpose equipment self-made by the participating team. It is used to monitor the motion and status of the robot, control the robot's actions, receive game-related information and robot image transmission from the Referee System event engine server, and can send event-specific interactive instructions to the event engine server to expand the possibility of human-computer interaction.
p041-u011: A typical Custom Terminal can be composed of a display device, a computing platform (including memory, controller and arithmetic unit) and a set of input devices; it can also be integrated, such as a handheld tablet device with a network port.
p041-u012: Example: A team created a Custom Terminal, which can receive the robot's image transmission and display it on a self-made display. At the same time, a self-made UI displayed through an unofficial link is superimposed, and the robot can be controlled through a matching controller. As a result, the team can complete the game without using the official Referee System player terminal and Remote Controller.
p041-u013: All Custom Terminals in the Operator Room can be wired to connect and communicate with each other, and the Custom Terminals can be wired to the event engine server and send and receive relevant content through the RJ45 interface set in the Operator Room.
p041-u014: Custom Terminal can receive event information displayed on the Referee System player terminal and accessible to oneself, such as: HP of both parties, one's own economy, remaining time of the game, and key events of the game, etc.
p041-u015: A Custom Terminal can send match instructions supported by the Referee System player terminal, such as selecting a Performance System before a match or redeeming Projectile Allowance during a match,
p042-u002: The core competition area of the Infantry Match is called the ‘Battlefield’. It is a 5 m long by 5 m wide area containing separate Starting Zones and bunkers for the Red and Blue sides. For details on projectiles and the Operator Room, see ‘3.2.5.1 Projectiles’ and ‘3.2.5.2 Operator Room’.

p045-u003: In the Infantry Match, each time a robot deals projectile damage to the opponent, it recovers HP equal to 50% of the damage dealt.
p045-u005: The Infantry Match has two stages: a group round-robin stage and a knockout stage. The group round-robin format is BO2, and the knockout format is BO3.
p045-u006: The following are the winning conditions for a single game:
p045-u008: When the HP of one robot drops to 0, the game ends immediately and the opponent wins.
p045-u010: When the game time runs out, and neither side's HP is 0, the robot with the higher remaining HP wins.
p045-u012: When the time of a game runs out, the HP of both sides is not 0, and the remaining HP of the robots is the same, the side whose HP was deducted later for the first time wins.
p045-u014: When the time of a game runs out, and both sides' HP is not 0, and both sides are at full health, the side with the higher total amount of ammunition will win.
p045-u016: When the time of a game runs out, if the HP of both sides is not 0, both are full health and the total amount of bullets fired is the same, the side that fired the first bullet earlier wins.
p045-u018: If the above conditions cannot determine victory, it will be considered a draw.
p045-u021: If the score between two teams in the knockout stage is 0:1 or 1:0, the one who wins 1 game will win.
p045-u023: If two teams in the knockout stage have a score of 0:0 or 1:1, compare their time-averaged net remaining HP across the rounds completed to date; the team with the higher value wins.
p045-u025: If the divisional Infantry Match schedule includes two group-stage rounds, compare only the teams’ average net remaining HP per round from the start of the second group-stage round through the matches completed to date.
p045-u027: If two teams have the same time-averaged net remaining HP and the winner cannot be determined, the Organizing Committee will determine the winner by an on-site draw to ensure that the subsequent schedule proceeds smoothly.

p047-u002: The inspection results of Pre-Match Inspection and adaptive training are for reference only and do not serve as the basis for passing the inspection for the official competition.
p047-u004: The inspection results of official matches are only effective for that match.
p047-u006: Passing inspection only proves that the robot met the inspection pass criteria at the time of inspection; the team must itself ensure that the robot always meets the Robot Building Specifications Manual requirements. During inspection, all robot functions must be proactively demonstrated to the inspectors.
p047-u007: To ensure that the robot produced by the participating team meets the requirements of the "RoboMaster 2027 University Series Robot Building Specifications Manual"
p047-u008: For Pre-Match Inspection, teams in the 3V3 Match and Infantry Match must arrive at the inspection area 60 minutes and 40 minutes in advance, respectively. The inspection process is as follows:
p047-u009: Each robot can be brought into the inspection area by a maximum of 2 team members, and another team member or supervising teacher is responsible for organizing and cooperating with the pre-match inspection. No other team members are allowed to enter the inspection area without the approval of the Chief Inspector. If the participating robot does not arrive at the inspection area, no member of the participating team is allowed to enter the inspection area.
p047-u010: The participating team members bring the robot into the inspection area
p047-u012: Staff mark each robot to be inspected (including, but not limited to, a PASS card, a timestamp written to the Referee System onboard module, or Qingliu lineup registration) and update the mark according to which inspection items it passes. Only robots with a complete mark may enter the waiting area and competition area. Teams must correct robots that fail inspection until they meet the inspection requirements. Teams must also check and confirm that the Referee System onboard module’s structure and functions are normal.
p047-u014: The captain signs to confirm the inspection results
p047-u015: After the team leader signs and confirms, no objection may be raised to the inspection results.
p047-u017: In RMUL's 3V3 competition, each participating team can borrow the Referee System of at most one spare robot.
p047-u019: After completing Pre-Match Inspection, a participating team must arrive at the waiting area at least 10 minutes before each match. In the 3V3 Match, each team may have at most 10 field personnel; in the Infantry Match, at most 4. One field member must wear the ‘Captain’ armband and perform the captain’s duties. If the team needs to repair a robot after entering the waiting area, it must obtain referee approval. The robot may leave the waiting area for repair only after waiting-area staff remove its PASS card. After repair, the robot must return to the inspection area and pass Pre-Match Inspection again before returning to the waiting area. If the robot is late to the waiting area as a result, it may not compete, and the participating team bears the consequences.
p048-u000: ‘Captain’ armband: Any field team member wearing a ‘Captain’ armband performs the captain’s duties during the match. The captain manages the team’s match procedure, confirms results, submits Team Technical Timeout requests, files Appeals, and so on.
p048-u001: After the team is sent from the waiting area to the field, it enters the field’s waiting zone and places its robots there. Once the referee approves, the team carries the robots to the Battlefield entrance and stands by. The referee opens the door and guides team members onto the field according to the match procedure. The Setup Period countdown starts as the door opens.
p048-u003: The Setup Period is 3 minutes for the 3V3 Match and 2 minutes for the Infantry Match. During it, field team members place robots in their respective Starting Zones, check that the Referee System is operating normally, preload projectiles and debug the modular 42mm launching mechanism. They may repair robots or replace equivalent parts in accordance with the specifications. In the 3V3 Match, they must debug robots in their side’s designated debugging zone; in the Infantry Match, they may debug only inside the Starting Zone. Each team may have only one field team member leave the designated debugging zone to debug.
p048-u004: [1] Red team designated debugging area [2] Blue team designated debugging area
p048-u007: Equivalent parts: standard modules or parts with the same material, shape and function, such as model motors and self-made friction wheel modules
p049-u000: and so on. The main structure that carries the robot body, such as its chassis, cannot be replaced by an equivalent part.
p049-u002: If the ‘equivalent parts’ include Referee System onboard modules, the participating team must ensure that those modules function normally (including version, sensor calibration and installation specifications). An abnormality in an onboard module included in the ‘equivalent parts’ does not trigger an Official Technical Pause.
p049-u003: When there is 1 minute and 30 seconds left in the preparation phase, it is recommended that the Operator enter the Operator Room to complete the debugging of the keyboard and mouse, and check to confirm that the robot control and official equipment are operating normally. If the official equipment cannot operate normally, Battlefield personnel must request it before there are 15 seconds left in the preparation phase, otherwise the referee will not grant a technical timeout. Except for the Operator corresponding to the robot on the field, other Battlefield personnel are not allowed to enter the Operator Room.
p049-u004: When there are 30 seconds left in the preparation phase, all robots in the Battlefield need to be powered on, unpowered robots need to be moved out of the Battlefield, and everyone in the Battlefield must leave in an orderly manner.
p049-u005: At the end of the Setup Period, field personnel must place the Sentry Robot’s debugging Remote Controller in the designated area at the Battlefield entrance.
p049-u007: During the preparation phase, when the Referee System or Operator Room equipment fails (fault conditions are shown in the table below) or when the robot needs to be temporarily inspected, the Head Referee can initiate an official technical pause and pause countdown. The suspension initiation time is determined by the Head Referee depending on the situation.
p049-u008: During an Official Technical Pause, field team members must cooperate with the referees to resolve faults related to the Referee System or official equipment, and may not repair other faults.
p049-u009: If the Referee System fails and must be replaced, the replacement must comply with the time limit for replacing the Referee System onboard module in the RoboMaster 2027 University Series Robot Building Specifications Manual.
p049-u010: After the Referee System or official equipment fault is resolved and the Head Referee resumes the countdown, field team members must follow the three-minute Setup Period requirements and leave the Battlefield at the specified time.
p049-u022: Because it is impossible to determine whether a failure is in the Referee System onboard module itself, caused by defects in the participating robot’s electrical or structural design, or caused by robot combat in an earlier match, Routine Battle Damage—except for the Regulation 3 case above—does not trigger an Official Technical Pause. The Referee will provide a spare Referee System onboard module. The participating team may request a Team Technical Pause to repair the robot.
p049-u023: If, after investigation by the referee, the fault conditions described in Regulations 2 and 3 above are caused by the participating team, the referee will explain the situation and end the official technical suspension.
p050-u001: If the robot’s mechanical structure or software system, or the keyboard, mouse or other equipment brought into the Operator Room, fails, the participating team may request a Team Technical Pause only before the Setup Period’s 15-second countdown. The captain must apply to a referee in the Battlefield or Operator Room and state the requested pause duration and reason. Once the request is made and communicated to the Head Referee, it cannot be canceled or changed.
p050-u002: Once the Head Referee confirms a Team Technical Pause, the Referee notifies both teams at the same time, regardless of which side requested it.
p050-u003: After the Head Referee confirms that both teams are ready, the technical pause may end early. Even if a team does not enter the Battlefield or the pause ends early, the opportunity consumed is still the one corresponding to the duration declared by the team when it applied.
p050-u004: To ensure that the subsequent schedule runs on time, both sides together may initiate only 1 Team Technical Pause during the same Setup Period, on a first-come, first-served basis. The post-match result confirmation form records whether any technical-pause opportunity was consumed during the match.
p050-u005: In both the 3V3 Match and Infantry Match, each participating team has two opportunities to request a 2-minute Team Technical Pause.
p050-u007: After the Setup Period, the match enters the 15-Second Referee System Self-Check Period. During the self-check, the Referee System server automatically checks the Referee System Client connection, the robots’ Referee System onboard module status and the Field Props status, and resets all robots’ HP to ensure they start the match at full HP.
p050-u009: After the 15-Second Referee System Self-Check Period, the match enters the Five-Second Countdown. During this time, the Referee System Client does not respond to robot control commands, including those from Custom Terminals. When the countdown ends, the Client resumes responding to control commands and the match starts immediately.
p050-u011: Robots engage in shooting combat in the core competition area, the Battlefield.
p050-u013: A Round ends when its time expires or a team triggers a Victory Condition early. A Match ends when a winner is determined or all its Rounds have been completed.
p050-u015: For each Match, the Referee records on the result confirmation form the main penalties in each Round, key settlement information at the end of the match, the result and the use of Team Technical Pause opportunities.
p051-u000: The captain must sign to confirm the match result within 5 minutes after the Match ends. If the captain neither signs nor files an Appeal within 5 minutes, the result is deemed confirmed.
p051-u002: After a 3V3 Match, the participating team must power off its robots, carry them off the Battlefield and take them to the projectile-clearing area. There, following staff instructions, it must return all armbands and PASS cards, remove all projectiles from the robots, and return all projectiles used in the match. After an Infantry Match, the team must carry out these exit procedures on the field.
p052-u001: To ensure fair competition and discipline, participating teams, participants and robots must strictly follow the competition rules. Referees issue appropriate penalties for violations. Some penalties issued before the match officially starts take effect after it starts.
p052-u002: Major penalties and all appeals during the game will be announced.
p052-u003: The penalties corresponding to all the violations in this chapter will be determined by the Head Referee based on the actual situation of the game. If there are situations during the game that affect the fairness of the game but are not covered by the penalty details and serious violations, the Head Referee will make a decision based on the actual situation.
p052-u004: If one party's behavior directly causes the other party to commit a violation, it will not be regarded as a violation by the other party, but the other party must terminate the violation in a timely manner.
p052-u007: During the event, the Referee System or referee will penalize participants and robots that do not comply with the rules of the event. The penalties are as follows:
p052-u018: The types of manual penalties during the game are as shown in the following table:
p053-u002:
- If the violating robot is a Sentry Robot, its chassis power is cut for 2 s, and the operator interfaces of the other robots are obscured for 2 s.
- If the violating robot is not a Sentry Robot, its operator interface is obscured for 5 s, and the operator interfaces of the other robots are obscured for 2 s.
- The Referee System automatically deducts 15% of the violating robot’s current Max HP, and the other surviving robots each have 5% of their current Max HP deducted. If a robot receives another Yellow Card Warning within 30 s after a Yellow Card Warning, the percentage of its current Max HP deducted is twice the previous percentage; the other surviving robots each have 5% of their current Max HP deducted.
- In each round, when a robot accumulates 3 Yellow Card Warnings, it also receives a Red Card Warning.
Two-side Yellow Card: The operator interfaces of all Operators are obscured for 2 s, and all robots have 5% of their Max HP deducted. This is not counted toward any single robot’s accumulated Yellow Card count.
Note: If Yellow Card Warnings are received consecutively, the operator-interface obscuring times are added together and the 30 s timer is reset. If a robot’s remaining HP is less than or equal to the HP deducted by a penalty, its HP is reduced to 1. The chassis power-cut and operator-interface obscuring durations caused by violation penalties are independent of the match mechanisms and are not added to them.
p053-u004:
- Robot Ejection:
  - If a robot is Ejected before the 15-Second Referee System Self-Check Period, it may not take the field and must be removed from the Battlefield. No other robot may substitute for it in any remaining round of that Match.
  - If a robot is Ejected during the 15-Second Referee System Self-Check Period, the Red Card Warning is issued after the match starts.
  - If a robot is Ejected during a match, its HP immediately becomes 0, its video feed and multi-robot communication are disconnected, and it cannot undergo Revival.
- Ejection of field team members: The Referee requires the Ejected person to leave the competition area immediately. No other field team member may replace them in any remaining round of that Match. The robot controlled by an Ejected Operator is also Ejected for the current round and may not take the field in any remaining round of that Match; no other robot may substitute for it.
p054-u003:
If a Loss by forfeit penalty is issued for one round (hereinafter ‘round forfeit’), the detailed rules are as follows:
3V3 Match:
- If the forfeit penalty is issued before the five-minute Round, including during the Setup Period and the 15-Second Referee System Self-Check Period, the violating side’s Control Points are 0, its remaining robots have full HP, and the other side’s Control Points and robot HP are full. The round time is regarded as 300 s.
- If the forfeit penalty is issued during the five-minute Round, the round ends immediately. The violating side’s Control Points are 0, its remaining robots’ HP is that at the end of the round, and the other side’s Control Points and robot HP are the values at the end of the round. The round time is the actual elapsed match time when the forfeit is issued.
- If the forfeit penalty is issued after the five-minute Round, the violating side’s Control Points are 0, its remaining robots’ HP is that at the end of the round, and the other side’s Control Points and robot HP are the values at the end of the round. The round time is the actual elapsed match time when the forfeit is issued.
Infantry Match:
- If the forfeit penalty is issued before the two-minute Round, including during the Setup Period and the 15-Second Referee System Self-Check Period, the violating side’s robot HP is 0 and the other side’s robot HP is full. The round time is regarded as 120 s.
- If the forfeit penalty is issued during the two-minute Round, the round ends immediately and both sides’ robot HP is that at the end of the round. The round time is the actual elapsed match time when the forfeit is issued.
- If the forfeit penalty is issued after the two-minute Round, both sides’ robot HP is that at the end of the round. The round time is the actual elapsed match time when the forfeit is issued.
If a Loss by forfeit penalty is issued for one match (hereinafter ‘match forfeit’), the penalty applies to all rounds of that match, and HP settlement for each round follows the descriptions above.

p058-u013: Violation penalty: Before the field is cleared, field team members must resolve safety issues at the referees’ request; otherwise, the violating robot may not take the field. If the issue arises during a match, issue a Verbal Warning; if it is ineffective, issue a Red Card Warning to the violating person or robot. If the safety hazard is serious, the Head Referee handles it according to ‘8 Abnormal Situations’.
p058-u014: R35 No robot may continuously launch projectiles outside of Battlefield.
p058-u015: Violation penalty: Verbal warning. If the warning is not valid, issue a red card warning for the offending robot.
p058-u016: R36 During the Setup Period and the 15-Second Referee System Self-Check Period, robots on the Battlefield must not leave their corresponding Starting Zones.
p058-u017: Violation penalties: Maximum red card warning for violating bots.
p058-u018: R37 During the Setup Period, any projectile that needs to be fired must be fired into the projectile-clearing bag provided by the referees.
p058-u019: Violation penalties: Maximum red card warning for violators and violating bots.
p058-u020: R38 During the race, the robot shall not be broken down into sub-robots or multiple subsystems connected by flexible cables, and shall not actively throw or launch its own parts.
p058-u021: Violation penalty: Issuing a red card warning to the violating robot.
p058-u022: R39 A subsystem or individual component resulting from disassembling a Heavy Robot must not leave the Workbench.
p058-u023: Violation penalties: Maximum red card warning for violating bots.
p058-u024: During the R40 competition, no surviving robot shall use its own structure to cover any Armor Module, nor shall it be deformed beyond the maximum stretch size.
p058-u025: Violation penalty: Issue a warning to the violating side based on subjective intent. If the concealment is deliberate, issue a Yellow Card Warning and a Verbal Warning when the violation occurs;
p059-u000: if the Verbal Warning is ineffective, issue a Red Card Warning. If the concealment is passive, issue one Yellow Card Warning when the violation occurs.
p059-u001: R41 In the preparation stage, the module or part replaced by the robot shall meet the requirements of "equivalent parts", see "5.3 Preparation stage" for details.
p059-u002: Violation penalties: Maximum red card warning for violating bots.
p059-u005: R42 A robot on one side may not use any of its own structures to ram the other robot. If the dead robot blocks the critical movement path, it can be slowly pushed away.
p059-u006: In a collision between Ground Robots, the violating robot is the one the referee determines to be the active party.
p059-u007: Violation penalty: Issuing a warning to the violating robot based on the subjective intention and the degree of impact.
p059-u015: If a collision causes serious consequences for the opposing robot or affects match fairness, the violating robot (by robot number only) may not take the field in the next round of the same competition stage, and no other robot may substitute for it.
p059-u016: R43 A robot must not, through active interference, blocking, ramming or similar actions, cause any of its own structures to become rigidly connected to the opposing robot.
p059-u017: Violation penalty: Start timing when a Rigid Connection can be identified. Warn the violating robot according to the duration of the violation. When the violation exceeds 10 s, issue the first Yellow Card Warning, then issue one Yellow Card Warning every 20 s until the violating robot is ejected. Regardless of whether the robot is Alive, if the violation lasts more than 90 s, the violating side is given a Loss by forfeit for the round at most, depending on its intent.
p059-u018: R44 A robot must not use any contact-based means to interfere with the opposing robot’s HP Recovery.
p059-u019: Violation Penalty: Issue a yellow card warning to the violating robot.
p060-u001: To ensure fair competition and that robots on the Battlefield can effectively obtain Buffs or supplies, supply Restricted Zones are established. One side’s Supply Zone is a supply Restricted Zone for the opposing side’s robots. Robots of one side or both sides, as applicable, must not enter a Restricted Zone, as shown in the figure.
p060-u004: R45 A robot from one side shall not enter the supply restricted area.
p060-u005: Violation penalty: Issue a warning to the violating side according to the duration of the stay and the impact of the violation. When the violation exceeds 3 s, issue the first Yellow Card Warning, then one every 10 s until the robot is Defeated or abnormally offline. If staying in the Restricted Zone causes serious damage to an opposing robot, issue a Red Card Warning to the violating robot.
p060-u006: R46 Wireless debuggers and Movable Props used in the match must not be brought onto the field. During the match, robots may use only the official projectiles and Movable Props provided by the Organizing Committee on the field.
p060-u007: Violation penalty: The maximum disqualification of the violating party from the competition.
p060-u008: R47 During a match, robots must not damage Field Props or projectiles, or interfere with the normal operation of Field Props.
p060-u009: Violation penalty: The maximum disqualification of the violating party from the competition.
p061-u001: If the following behaviors occur during the competition, it will be judged as a serious violation. For serious violations, RMOC will disqualify the offending party from the competition up to the maximum. If the act violates local laws and regulations, RMOC will cooperate with relevant departments to pursue the legal responsibility of the violator.
p062-u001: there will be a certain delay in referee's manual punishment and handling of abnormal situations. If it has a significant impact on the competition results, Chief Referee will determine the final handling result according to the actual situation.
p062-u002: If the following abnormal situations occur, they will be handled according to the corresponding methods, and the teams of both parties shall not have any objections. The handling methods are as follows:
p062-u004: When serious safety hazards or abnormal conditions occur, such as battery deflagration, venue power failure, high-pressure gas cylinder explosion or on-site personnel conflict, etc., Head Referee will notify both Operators and penalize all robots through the Referee System. The results of the game will be invalidated and the game will restart after the hidden hazards or abnormalities are eliminated. RMOC will prioritize safety issues and will do its best to protect the robot to the extent possible, there is no guarantee that there will be no impact on the robot at all, and any loss or impact caused by safe disposal will be borne by the participating teams themselves.
p062-u006: During the match, if non-critical props on the Battlefield are damaged—for example, if the floor adhesive is damaged—in a way that does not affect the fairness of the match, the match proceeds normally.
p062-u008: During the match, if a robot’s Light Indicator has an abnormal lighting effect, the match proceeds normally.
p062-u010: During a match, if a key Battlefield prop has a logical or structural failure—for example, an abnormal network causes a robot to go offline or a Battlefield prop mechanism cannot operate normally—the Referee will handle the failure manually through the Referee System. If it cannot be handled manually, the Referee will notify both Operators and Eject all robots at the same time. The round ends immediately and its result is invalidated. The match restarts after the problem is resolved.
p062-u012: During a match, if abnormal operation or structural damage of a key Battlefield prop affects fairness and the Head Referee does not promptly confirm this and end the match, so that the match continues when it should have ended and produces a winner and loser, the Chief Referee will verify the matter within 5 minutes after the match ends. The round result is then invalidated and the round must be replayed.
p062-u014: If a serious violation clearly warrants a Loss by forfeit penalty but the Head Referee does not confirm and enforce it in time, the Chief Referee verifies it within 5 minutes after the match ends, voids that round’s result, and additionally issues a Loss by forfeit penalty to the violating side.
p062-u016: During the course of the game, if there are any situations that may affect the fairness of the game, within 5 minutes after the end of the game, Chief Referee will notify the captains of both sides of the situation and suspend the results confirmation process, and within 60 minutes thereafter, verify and inform the captains of both sides of the final treatment. Neither party can dispute the outcome.
p063-u001: Each participating team has 1 Appeal opportunity for each competition site and event in RMUL 2027; opportunities cannot be accumulated. If an Appeal succeeds, the opportunity is retained; otherwise, 1 opportunity is consumed. When no Appeal opportunities remain, the Arbitration Committee will no longer accept Appeals from that team. After accepting an Appeal, the Arbitration Committee arbitrates the submitted materials and relevant evidence. The Chief Referee informs both sides of the result on behalf of the Arbitration Committee, which has final authority to interpret the Appeal result.
p063-u002: The following are not grounds for appeal:
p063-u004: Verbal Warning, Yellow Card Warning and Red Card Warning in Violation Penalties.
p063-u006: The type and process for initiating a technical timeout.
p063-u008: The Referee System onboard module indicates ‘Routine Battle Damage’.
p063-u009: An Appeal may not be initiated more than 5 minutes after signing the result confirmation form or after a match ends.
p064-u001: A participating team that wishes to file an Appeal must follow this procedure:
p064-u002: Within 5 minutes after the match ends (according to the time recorded on the result confirmation form), teams in a group-stage match may appeal any round in that match, while the losing team in a knockout match may appeal any round it lost. The captain files the Appeal at the result confirmation desk; filing initiates the Appeal process and consumes an Appeal opportunity. The Arbitration Committee will not accept an Appeal after the team has signed the result confirmation form or more than 5 minutes after the match ends. Appeals are not allowed before or during a match.
p064-u003: The participating team files an Appeal
p064-u005: If the Appeal concerns robots belonging to both sides, the Arbitration Committee may isolate the relevant robots for testing. At the latest, the isolated robots will be returned with the Appeal result.
p064-u006: After receiving an Appeal form, the appealing team’s captain must complete it in detail and submit it with a signature at the result confirmation desk within 10 minutes. In addition to the captain, at most 2 field team members may assist. The Arbitration Committee arbitrates only the ‘Grounds for Appeal’ section, which the appealing team may not later modify or supplement. If the form is not signed and submitted within 10 minutes, it is deemed to contain no grounds for appeal, the remaining process is skipped, and the result is deemed to maintain the original match result.
p064-u007: The participating team completes and signs the Appeal form
p064-u008: If either side needs to collect Appeal materials, it must submit them to the Chief Referee within 30 minutes after the Appeal is accepted, and agree in advance on the time and place of submission. The materials must be explained in detail when submitted.
p064-u009: The participating team collects evidence or materials for its defense
p064-u010: The Arbitration Committee will not accept new materials after the submission deadline. The process may proceed directly to the next step if neither side needs to collect materials, the Arbitration Committee has sufficient evidence, or the stated grounds for Appeal cannot be used as a basis for an Appeal.
p064-u011: After ruling on the relevant evidence, the Arbitration Committee notifies both captains to come to the arbitration room, where it presents the basis for its ruling and informs them of the Appeal result. Both sides must arrive within 10 minutes of notification. This step is in person only. No more than 3 people from each side may attend, and attendees must be Official Team Members or Advisor Teachers. If either side is absent, it is deemed to have waived participation. If the appealing side’s grounds clearly do not match the facts or cannot be used as grounds for an Appeal, the Arbitration Committee may explain the situation only to that side and maintain the original match result. Proceed to the next step when both representatives accept the Appeal result or the Arbitration Committee considers the necessary communication complete.
p064-u012: Inform both sides of the Appeal result
p064-u013: The Arbitration Committee records the appeal result on the appeal form. One member from each side present in the arbitration room must sign as that side’s representative. By signing, they acknowledge the result, and neither side may object afterward. If the representative does not sign within 5 minutes after the result is given, the result is considered acknowledged. If the appealing side’s reason clearly does not match the facts or cannot be used as grounds for appeal, the Arbitration Committee explains the situation to that side and maintains the original match result; the appealed side need not sign and is considered to have acknowledged the result.
p064-u015: If a round is replayed because an Appeal ruling requires both sides to replay, a team that still has an Appeal opportunity may appeal the replayed round after it ends. If the original appealing team files another Appeal (a ‘continuing Appeal’), it consumes that team’s Appeal opportunity regardless of whether the Appeal succeeds, because it would seriously affect the schedule.
p064-u019: Materials submitted by a participating team for an Appeal must be no larger than 500 MB per file and may include no more than 10 files.
p065-u001: Appeal results include maintaining the original match result, a Loss by forfeit for the respondent, or a replay by both sides. After the Arbitration Committee confirms the Appeal result, neither side may object.
p065-u003: Successful Appeal: the respondent receives a Loss by forfeit, or both sides replay the match.
p065-u005: Unsuccessful Appeal: the original match result is maintained.
p065-u006: If, during the Arbitration Committee’s communication step, both sides are told to replay but neither accepts, the Appeal is unsuccessful and the original match result is maintained.
p065-u008: Provided the overall schedule is not affected, a replay is generally scheduled after all matches that day have ended; the actual schedule governs.
p065-u010: The replay follows the regular match procedure. Both sides must play at the time specified by the Organizing Committee and comply with the relevant rules.
p065-u011: If the Appeal result affects the win-loss result of the match, the match result must be determined again.
p065-u012: Example: The original BO3 match result is 1:2: Red won Round 1, and Blue won Rounds 2 and 3. After the match, Red appeals Round 2, and the Appeal result requires both sides to replay that round. If Red wins the replay, the final match result is 2:0; if Blue wins the replay, the final result is 1:2.
p066-u002: Pre-inspection is a check performed before formal Pre-Match Inspection to help teams find and resolve robot problems in advance. RMOC will do its best to help teams troubleshoot and handle robot faults during pre-inspection and adaptation training, but a pre-inspection result is not equivalent to the formal match inspection result. If a robot does not meet the inspection pass criteria during formal inspection, it may not compete.
p066-u005: 3V3 Match: Each team may bring at most 4 robots for pre-inspection.
p066-u007: Infantry Match: In each event, each team may bring at most 2 robots for pre-inspection.
p066-u009: Adaptation training is a debugging and familiarization opportunity for participating teams before the formal match. Its main purposes include:
p066-u011: Familiarity with the match environment and procedure.
p066-u013: Testing and adjusting robot status and strategy.
p066-u016: 3V3 Match: 15 minutes total, divided between 1 round and free debugging time.
p066-u018: Infantry Match: 10 minutes total, divided between 1 round and free debugging time. A team participating in both the 3V3 Match and Infantry Match may attend adaptation training only for the 3V3 Match.
p066-u021: The training schedule is compact and focused on debugging. By default, training is not paused unless major official equipment fails.
p066-u023: If an onboard Referee System anomaly occurs, the RMOC may grant an official technical pause of up to 2 minutes to address the fault; this pause counts toward the total adaptive-training time.
p066-u025: Team Technical Pauses are not available during adaptation training.
p066-u026: Rules for the free debugging stage:
p066-u028: For projectile-firing tests, a participating team may ask the Referee to lend it a projectile-clearing bag and may fire only into that bag.
p066-u030: The Round status of the free debugging stage is "not started", and the participating teams need to adapt themselves and be familiar with the switching and requirements of each stage of the competition.
p067-u002: Robots that fail to pass the inspection on time or have safety hazards are not allowed to participate in adaptive training.
p067-u004: Robots that do not pass the inspection due to serious non-compliance with the inspection criteria are only allowed to participate in the free debugging stage in adaptive training.
p067-u006: The number of robots participating in adaptive training must not exceed the maximum robot lineup limit specified in each competition.
